h1: The 7 Best Patio Heaters Under $200, Propane and Electric, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Patio Heaters Under $200: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 7 propane and electric patio heaters under $200, scored on BTU output, coverage, tilt safety, base stability and weather rating.
summary: The Hykolity 50,000 BTU with the weight-adjustable sand box base is the best patio heater under $200 for stability, pairing high output with a stainless burner and tip-over protection. The Sweetcrispy 48,000 BTU adds a side table, the Amazon Basics 46,000 BTU is the brand-name option, and the DR. INFRARED is the electric choice for covered spaces.
intro: Patio heater marketing leans on one number, BTU, and ignores the more important one: stability. A tall heater with a propane tank at its base is top-heavy, and wind or a bump from a chair is what knocks it over. Heat output matters only if the heater stays upright, which is why the base design and tilt shutoff say more about a heater than the BTU rating.

Seven heaters are ranked below, five propane and two electric. All sit in the $100 to $200 bracket. Scoring weights output, coverage, tilt and flame-out safety, base design and assembly. Coverage figures are the makers' own claims, and real warmth drops sharply in wind or open space.

products.name: Hykolity 50,000 BTU Propane Patio Heater With Sand Box
products.verdict: 50,000 BTU with a double-layer 304 stainless burner, a weight-adjustable base and tip-over protection.
products.description:
The Hykolity Sand Box model puts out 50,000 BTU through a double-layer 304 stainless steel burner and heats up to 200 sq ft. It uses a conical, weight-adjustable tank base tested to 26.45 lbs, and a tip-over protection system.

It wins because the base is where heaters fail. A sand-fillable base lets you add weight, which lowers the centre of gravity, and the tip-over system cuts the gas if the heater leans. Double-layer 304 stainless is the grade used for outdoor fixtures because it resists rust. The 50,000 BTU figure is the highest in the ranking. The cost is weight when filled, which makes it harder to move.

Buy it if you want output and stability. Skip it if you will relocate it daily.
products.idealFor: Windy patios needing a stable heater.

products.name: Sweetcrispy 48,000 BTU Propane Patio Heater
products.verdict: 48,000 BTU, flame-out and 45 degree tilt shutoff, a built-in side table, wheels and ground anchors.
products.description:
The Sweetcrispy delivers 48,000 BTU through a double-layer 304 stainless burner and claims an 18-foot diameter for 4 to 8 people. It has flame-out cutoff, a tilt sensor that acts past 45 degrees, a built-in side table, wheels and ground anchors.

The side table is a nice touch for drinks. Wheels let one person roll it, and ground anchors let you fix it down on a deck. It ranks second because its base is less adjustable than the Hykolity's sand box, and the 18-foot coverage claim is optimistic: expect warmth within a few feet.

Buy it if you want a table and wheels. Skip it if stability against wind is the top need.

products.name: Hykolity 50,000 BTU Propane Patio Heater With Triple Protection
products.verdict: A 50,000 BTU table-design heater with wheels and an under-an-hour assembly.
products.description:
This Hykolity gives 50,000 BTU through a stainless burner, in a table design with wheels, heating up to 200 sq ft, with assembly in under an hour.

A table design hides the tank in the base and gives you a surface, which is a more domestic look than a bare pole. It ranks third because the listing's headline is triple protection but the detail is thinner than the sand box model's.

Buy it if you want a tidy table-style look. Skip it if you want the weight-adjustable base.
products.idealFor: A tidy look on a small patio.
products.skipIf: You want a sand box base.

products.name: NEWBULIG 48,000 BTU Propane Patio Heater
products.verdict: An 87 inch pole with 48,000 BTU, 45 degree anti-tilt, flame-out protection, wheels and anchors.
products.description:
The NEWBULIG stands 87 inches tall, delivers 48,000 BTU, claims 18-foot coverage for 4 to 8 people and has 45 degree anti-tilt, flame-out protection, wheels and ground anchors.

Height pushes warmth down over a wider area, which suits larger groups. It ranks fourth because a tall pole is the least stable design, and the listing offers no sand base or wide stance.

Buy it if you seat a crowd in a sheltered space. Skip it if wind is a problem.

products.name: Amazon Basics 46,000 BTU Portable Propane Patio Heater
products.verdict: 46,000 BTU, 9-foot radius, a water tank base, a tilt auto-shutoff valve and a tank chain.
products.description:
The Amazon Basics heater provides 46,000 BTU over a 9-foot radius, uses a water tank base, has a tilt safety auto-shutoff valve and includes a chain to secure the propane tank.

A water-filled base adds weight like sand does, and the tank chain keeps the cylinder from shifting. It ranks fifth because the output is a little lower and the listing has no stainless-grade detail.

Buy it if you want a retailer-backed heater. Skip it if you want higher BTU.
products.idealFor: Buyers who prefer a house brand.

products.name: DR. INFRARED Portable Infrared Patio Heater 1500W
products.verdict: Selectable 900, 1200 or 1500W with IP55 weather rating, remote control and wall and ceiling brackets.
products.description:
The DR. INFRARED offers 900, 1200 or 1500W settings, an IP55 rating for indoor and outdoor use, a remote control with no thermostat, and wall and ceiling brackets. It runs on a standard 120V outlet.

Infrared electric heat warms people directly rather than the air, which works well under a pergola or a porch roof. IP55 means it resists dust and water jets. It ranks sixth because 1500W covers a small area and needs an outlet.

Buy it if you have a covered seating area near power. Skip it if you want open-air heat.

products.name: Hykolity 38.5 Inch 1500W Infrared Electric Patio Heater
products.verdict: A 1500W infrared heater with dual carbon tubes, 2 heat levels, a 24 hour timer and IP44, ETL certification.
products.description:
The Hykolity 38.5 inch heater uses 1500W dual carbon tubes with 2 heat levels, a 0 to 24 hour timer, an IP44 rating and ETL certification.

ETL certification means it was tested to a recognised electrical safety standard, which matters for a heater. A timer prevents leaving it on all night. It ranks last because IP44 is a lower weather rating than the DR. INFRARED's IP55 and heat is limited to a small seating cluster.

Buy it if you want a timer and a certified electric heater. Skip it if the area is exposed to rain.

whatMatters.detail: A tall heater with a top-heavy tank tips in wind. A sand or water base, ground anchors and a wide stance help. Look for a weight-adjustable base like the Hykolity sand box.
A tilt sensor cuts gas if the heater leans past about 45 degrees, and flame-out protection shuts off fuel if the flame dies. Both should be listed. Skip any propane heater without them.
More than 40,000 BTU is typical for a standing propane heater. Coverage claims such as an 18-foot diameter are best case; real warmth is within a few feet and shrinks in wind.
Propane suits open patios and needs a tank, while infrared electric suits covered areas near an outlet. Electric heats people directly and cannot warm a large open space.
IP55 resists dust and water jets, while IP44 resists splashes. Match the rating to your exposure. Cover propane heaters when not in use.

faq.q: Can I use a patio heater under a covered porch?
faq.a: Propane heaters need ventilation and should not be used in enclosed spaces. Check the manual for clearance from roofs. Electric infrared suits covered areas.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake when buying one?
faq.a: Buying on BTU alone. Stability and safety cutoffs matter more. Choose a heavy, anchored base.

faq.q: Is the Hykolity sand box worth it over the Sweetcrispy?
faq.a: For windy sites, yes, since you can add weight. If you want a table and wheels, the Sweetcrispy is more convenient.

faq.q: How long does a propane tank last?
faq.a: At about 50,000 BTU, a standard 20 lb tank lasts roughly 9 to 10 hours, since a pound of propane holds about 21,000 BTU. Keep a spare.
Allow an hour with two people. Check every fitting for leaks with soapy water before lighting.
Disconnect the tank, keep it outside and upright, and cover the heater. Do not store tanks indoors.

finalTake: The Hykolity 50,000 BTU Patio Heater with Sand Box is the best patio heater under $200, with the highest output, a weight-adjustable base and tip-over protection. The Sweetcrispy adds a side table and wheels, and the Amazon Basics is the house-brand pick. For covered spaces, the DR. INFRARED electric heater is the better fit. Always check the base and shutoffs first.
